page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a bare metal server featuring an Intel Xeon 2388G processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It delivers 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, offering substantial local capacity. There are no GPUs included in this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with the stress-ng single-core test and Geekbench single-core score placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance and database operations fall into the average tier. Notably, the PassMark memory score ranks in the top 10%, though large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidth benchmarks show weaker performance, placing in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks are highly efficient, while LLM inference speeds for small models show strong text generation capabilities.

As a dedicated bare metal instance, this server offers high resource density and predictable performance without virtualization overhead, representing a solid qualitative value for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. The combination of 128 GB RAM and a 3840 GB NVMe SSD makes it well-suited for database hosting, memory-cached applications, static web serving, and software compilation pipelines.
